note: From San Francisco Recreation and Park Department pages, Gardens of Golden Gate Park, San Francisco Public Works and SFMTA project pages, with a source on every item. department.name: San Francisco Recreation and Park Department
department.address: McLaren Lodge, Golden Gate Park, 501 Stanyan Street, San Francisco, CA 94117
department.what: Runs the city's parks, playgrounds, recreation centers and clubhouses, nine public pools, six golf courses (one of them, Sharp Park, is in Pacifica), Golden Gate Park, Camp Mather, the Randall Museum and Sharon Art Studio, and quarterly recreation classes. Street repaving, sewer and streetscape work is done by San Francisco Public Works; street safety, parking and transit projects by the SFMTA.

registration.label: Search and register for classes (Rec and Park online registration)
registration.note: Registration opens quarterly: the department's FAQ says it usually opens in August for fall, December for winter, March for spring and day camp, and May for summer. Last year, winter class registration opened Saturday, December 13, 2025 at 10 am (Rec and Park eNews, Dec 10, 2025). Exact winter 2027 dates were not posted on any page we could open as of November 4, 2026. Create an account first (your email is your login), then register online, by phone at 628-652-2900, or at a walk-in site during the registration period. For most courses you can still register by phone after a course starts, but late registration is not prorated. Swim passes and memberships are sold through the same system (sfrecpark.org/register).

projects.title: Portsmouth Square renovation (Chinatown)
projects.summary: The Mayor broke ground on the renovation in 2026. Rec and Park's construction update of October 30, 2026 says the new temporary walkway connecting the garage elevator is complete. No sewer replacement work is scheduled from October 8 to November 10, 2026, and that work was moved to after spring 2027; an October update reported an unforeseen pavement support issue on Walter U. Lum Place. Earlier, in late July and August 2026, Kearny Street had lane and weekend closures while the pedestrian bridge was demolished.

projects.title: Outdoor fitness and recreation area for seniors (Golden Gate Park Senior Center)
projects.summary: Rec and Park broke ground October 6, 2026 on a 5,000 square foot outdoor area at the Golden Gate Park Senior Center: stationary exercise equipment for up to 20 people, open space for dance, tai chi, yoga and classes, shaded seating under a pergola, an accessible picnic table and pathway, and four refreshed accessible parking spaces. The design came from four community meetings and two multilingual surveys in 2024 and 2025. No completion date was given.

projects.title: Folsom Streetscape (2nd to 11th Streets)
projects.summary: Public Works update of October 27, 2026: crews are on punch-list items and final installations. Done so far: 32 of 33 new trees, benches, transit boarding islands between 6th and 9th Streets, and repaving from 2nd to 11th Streets. Decorative crosswalks were scheduled October 23 to 30; Clear Channel will install the remaining bus shelters. The project adds a two-way protected bikeway, landscaped median, raised crosswalks, rain gardens, and sewer and water main replacement.

source.label: SF Public Works, Folsom Streetscape (updated Oct 27, 2026)

projects.title: Pavement Renovation #90 and Sewer Replacement (18 blocks)
projects.summary: Sewer replacement, curb ramps, base repairs and repaving on 18 blocks including Granville Way, Jules Avenue, Corbett Avenue, Capitol Avenue, 23rd Street (Eureka to Diamond), Westwood Drive, Plymouth Avenue, Miramar Avenue, Marietta Drive, Funston Avenue, 14th and 15th Avenues, Noriega Street, 7th Avenue and Laguna Honda Boulevard. Work started August 2026 and runs about 16 months. Contractor: A. Ruiz Construction.

projects.title: Pavement Renovation No. 85 and Sewer Replacement (Western Addition, Marina, Cow Hollow, Laurel Heights, Outer Richmond, Haight Ashbury, Pacific Heights)
projects.summary: Sewer main relining and replacement, curb ramps, base repairs and repaving, summer 2026 to spring 2027. Work hours are usually 7 am to 5 pm weekdays. Curb, gutter, sidewalk and curb ramp work at four locations was paused in August 2026 because of a concrete supplier issue; no restart date is given. Contractor: Esquivel Grading and Paving.

projects.title: 13th Street Safety Project (13th Street and Duboce Avenue, Folsom to Valencia)
projects.summary: Protected bike lanes, sidewalk extensions, signal upgrades and repaving on 13th Street and Duboce Avenue between Folsom and Valencia, plus curb ramps and traffic islands at the US-101 off-ramp. Work runs 8 am to 4 pm weekdays (not holidays); barricades and lane reductions stay up after hours, and some bus stops move temporarily. The SFMTA warned of delays exiting the Mission Street/Duboce Avenue off-ramp for about four weeks.

source.label: SFMTA transit and traffic advisory, Oct 29 to Nov 4, 2026

projects.title: Potrero Yard Modernization (SFMTA bus yard)
projects.summary: The SFMTA is replacing the century-old bus yard at 2500 Mariposa Street with a four-story bus maintenance and storage facility; Webcor leads construction, which runs through 2030. Expect lane shifts and parking restrictions in the area bounded by Mariposa, Bryant, 17th and Hampshire Streets. Work hours are 7 am to 8 pm weekdays, with some overnight (11 pm to 4 am) and weekend work.

projects.title: Hayes Valley Pay or Permit Parking Expansion
projects.summary: The SFMTA Board approved the expansion on June 2, 2026. Redesigned test signs are up on Rose Street (Market to Octavia) and on Linden and Fell Streets west of Patricia's Green. The SFMTA says the project is on schedule for early 2027; no enforcement start date is given.

seasonal.title: Winter hours at the Golden Gate Park gardens
seasonal.detail: From the first Sunday in November through January, the San Francisco Botanical Garden's last entry is 4 pm; the Japanese Tea Garden's last entry is 4:30 pm from November to February. The Conservatory of Flowers is open 10 am to 4:30 pm and closed Wednesdays.

seasonal.title: New holiday ice rink at Fisherman's Wharf
seasonal.detail: A 6,300 square foot outdoor rink at 80 Jefferson Street, announced by the Port of San Francisco and run by On Ice Rinks LLC, is set to open November 4, 2026 and run through January 18, 2027, daily 10 am to 11 pm. Tickets at SanFranciscoOnIce.com.
seasonal.review_note: News report from September; the Port's own announcement was not opened, and the rink is Port property, not Rec and Park.

seasonal.title: Illuminate LIVE season wrapping up

seasonal.title: Free sandbags from Public Works before winter storms
seasonal.detail: The National Weather Service expects a wetter than normal December to February. Public Works gives San Francisco businesses up to 10 free sandbags before and during severe rainstorms, Monday to Saturday, 8 am to 2 pm, at the operations yard gate at Marin and Kansas Streets; bring proof of business address. Clear leaves from sidewalks and drains from the sidewalk side and report blockages below the grate to 311.

seasonal.detail: Cleaning and maintenance between Evans and Sunnydale stations from midnight to 5 am, September to November 2026; work at the Gilman platform on Tuesdays, November 3 and November 10. Owl service is not affected.

seasonal.title: Lane shifts around Potrero Yard
seasonal.detail: Week of October 29 to November 4: trenching on Hampshire Street (17th to Mariposa) and Bryant Street (18th to 16th); sidewalk excavation on 17th Street (Bryant to Hampshire), Mariposa Street (Potrero Avenue to Florida) and Bryant Street (18th to 16th); vault setting and conduit on Mariposa (Hampshire to Bryant). Work hours 7 am to 8 pm weekdays, with some overnight work from 11 pm to 4 am. The SFMTA posts a new notice each week.

seasonal.detail: Public Works crews began work on 14th and 15th Avenues on October 5, 2026, expected to finish by the end of October barring rain or unforeseen issues. Liaison: Alex Murillo, 628-271-2244.

seasonal.title: Public Works so far in 2026
seasonal.detail: Through October 2026, Public Works reports 447 blocks resurfaced, 5,144 potholes filled, 352 curb ramps installed, 18,958 trees pruned and 17,773 tons of debris collected. Report street problems to 311; the department aims to address its own issues within 48 hours on weekdays.
